name: TopTenarr
description: Scrapes public streaming Top 10 lists and syncs them as Plex Collections, pinned to your Plex home. Netflix is free; Pro unlocks Disney+, Max, Prime Video, Hulu, Apple TV+, Paramount+ and Peacock. Optional Radarr/Sonarr auto-request for missing titles. SETUP — nothing else is required in this template. Install, open the WebUI, then: 1. Sign in with Plex (PIN-based, no password typed here). The FIRST Plex account to sign in becomes the permanent owner of this instance, so do this before exposing the port. 2. Pick your Plex server and libraries. 3. Toggle the services you want (Movies and Shows toggle independently). 4. Optional: add Radarr/Sonarr under Settings to auto-request missing titles. Enter those there, NOT here — the app stores API keys encrypted, a template variable would sit in plain text on your flash drive. 5. Set your sync schedule. Make sure TZ below is correct or your schedule will run in UTC.

paths.name: Config Storage
paths.description: EXAMPLE: /mnt/user/appdata/toptenarr Where the database, encryption key and cover art are kept. The default is correct for almost everyone — leave it. Back this folder up.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: EXAMPLE: 7474 The port you will browse to. Only change it if something else on your server already uses 7474.

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: EXAMPLE: America/Los_Angeles Your timezone. Already filled in for US Pacific — change it only if you are elsewhere. Other examples: America/Denver, America/Chicago, America/New_York, Europe/London, Australia/Sydney. Without this the container runs on UTC and your sync will fire at the wrong hour.

variables.name: License Key (Pro)
variables.description: EXAMPLE: OOOO0-IIII1-UUUU0-OOOO1 Optional. Leave BLANK unless you bought Pro — Netflix works free without it. You can also paste this later in the app under Settings, which is easier. The dashes are only there to make the key readable — typing it with or without them both work.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: EXAMPLE: 99 User ID the app runs as. 99 is Unraid's "nobody" and is correct — do not change this unless you know exactly why.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: EXAMPLE: 100 Group ID the app runs as. 100 is Unraid's "users" and is correct — do not change this unless you know exactly why.

variables.name: UMASK
variables.description: EXAMPLE: 022 Permissions mask for files the app writes. 022 is correct — leave it alone.
